findings.issue: The end-to-end test 25 (miss dominance) only asserts that each item stays within its cap (0 <= item <= 1 or 1+ε). That follows from capped() and clip() alone, so the test almost cannot fail. The generator also misses the cases the protocol requires. (1) `_cells` only ever congests cells 26-28 (line 40), so model P_2 episodes are never creditable and the creditable-B2 branches of P4-2, P5a-2 and P7a-2 are never exercised. (2) The real side has exactly one B1 and one B2 episode, so there are no multi-episode days. (3) P5c is not among the rows and both_q is always [] (lines 58-59, 73). As a result, J5Eval's P5c branch (metanet_j5_eval.py:97-100, incl. don_long) is executed by no test anywhere. (4) The required bound J5(out) − J5(ref) ≤ Σ w_r·max(0, ΔA_r)/Σ w_r, the s_0 comparison and the violation-share and P7b+P7c report are absent. The pure variant in test_metanet_v5.py:104 draws a t_c that it never uses.

Test 30(b) is largely tautological. The P4 assertion compares J.p4_items with values built from IT.p4_day, which is the very function J.p4_items calls internally. The P7a assertion only checks that taper(x, don) == x when |don| ≤ 45, which is a test of taper, not of the mapping. The docstring claims 'P5a D ... P8 extra flags', but neither is asserted. The protocol's equalities for the production evaluator (J5Eval.day_items) against the gate are never checked: D_i → P5c, index error ≤ 1 ⇔ gate P7b hit, per-day P8 flags, and P8g (ii) = 1 exactly where the gate's P3 agrees and P8(iii) flags B_k. The checkpoint lists this as an open item.
findings.skeptic_reason: Confirmed by reading. tests/test_metanet_gate_refactor.py:274-275 builds the expected value with the same expression that metanet_j5.py:79-82 uses to implement p4_items (credit all True), so the P4 check is tautological. Nothing about P5a D, P5c D, P7b err≤1 ⇔ p7b_hit, the P8 spurious and extra flags or P8g(ii) is asserted, and J5Eval.day_items is never called. That falls short of §B10 test 30(b). Another reviewer's fuller check (scratchpad v5codereview/t30b_full.py), which runs day_items against the gate's per-day statistics on the synthetic worlds 101-110, gave 0 mismatches over P4 280, P5a 62, P7a 62, P5c 12, P7b 85, P7c 66 and P8g 140 comparisons. findings.issue: Test 30(b) is tautological. It never runs the production J5 evaluator (J5Eval.day_items) against the gate's per-day statistics. findings.issue: s1_ratio (P9 S1) returns a wrong value when the window [onset - 60 min, min(end, cut - 1)] has 1 or 2 bins. When seg is shorter than the 3-tap kernel, np.convolve(..., 'valid') swaps its arguments, so it returns 3 or 2 values equal to seg.sum()/3 instead of nothing. The refactor fixed only the 0-bin case (returns None, disclosed) and kept this latent case from the tag bit for bit.
findings.skeptic_reason:
Reproduced in venv314: IT.s1_ratio(np.full(100,1800.),50,60,1800.,cut) gives 1.0 (cut=41), 0.667 (cut=40, 2-bin window), 0.333 (cut=39, 1-bin window) and None (cut=38). When seg is shorter than the kernel, np.convolve 'valid' returns max(M,N)-min(M,N)+1 values, each equal to seg.sum()/3. So metanet_items.py:100 zero-pads the window, which contradicts v3 §5.4: "S1 = the maximum 3-bin rolling 15-min flow ... in [onset − 60 min, end]". The tag's `if roll.size else None` cannot catch this case.

Why it does not reach the recorded STOP:
- Real side: in the committed calibration facts (metanet_v5_precal_facts.json), 6 of 22 heavy-first days are truncated, and their real windows have 24-35 bins.
- Model side: the window is cut - ms + 12 bins, with cut >= rs + 12 on those days and |ms - rs| <= 18 bins (match_episodes tol_bins=18). So it has at least 6 bins.
- The screen's P9 failed on its count (n_matched 15 < required 17), and 11 other rows failed as well.

The defect is therefore latent for the validation gate only. It cannot reverse the stop and does not block launch.
findings.fix: In s1_ratio, return None when seg.size < 3, with the same disclosure as the empty-window fix. Extend test_s1_empty_window_returns_none to 1- and 2-bin windows (expect None). In test 30(a), count worlds that differ from the tag only through P9 on windows of fewer than 3 bins as disclosed fixes, the way crash worlds are counted. Record in the freeze audit that the defect is not outcome-relevant: give the calibration window sizes above and the P9 count failure.

Use cases with |Δonset| <= 45 min, and assert item·cap == min(|stat|, cap). findings.issue: Test 25 implements neither the miss-dominance bound nor the pre-registered report. Both variants (here and test_metanet_v5.py:96) only assert that each item lies in [0, cap], which holds by construction of capped()/taper(). The generator also never exercises matched B2 items or P5c.

findings.issue: Test 33 covers less than the protocol specifies. It does not run the §4.7 grid with its J_d selector, ensemble selection or the premise check. findings.skeptic_reason: I verified each claim in the test source. tests/test_metanet_j5_eval.py:_install (lines 92-95) stubs Q.model_day, Q.model_speeds and I.event_station. Before any re-run, extend test 33 to run the unstubbed readers (Q.model_day, I.event_station, the gate's _deterministic_rows) on a temporary Mayfly root that holds calibration-date files and one decoy validation-date directory. findings.issue: The gate guard only checks that the freeze-audit record exists. Any tracked, clean metanet_v5_freeze_audit.json passes. Nothing links the audit to the freeze record it audited: the audit names no freeze-record commit or blob, and nothing checks that it was committed after that record. Suppose a §B11.2 fix reverses the stop and the full re-run commits a new non-STOP freeze record (accepted when a fix record names it, lines 147-156). That record reaches the gate on the old audit of the STOP record, with no audit of its own.
findings.skeptic_reason: The facts hold. check() (metanet_v5_gate.py:145-146) only tests that the file is tracked and clean, and the audit names no freeze record. The tests stub `git log` with a single commit (test_metanet_gate_refactor.py:304, 336), so the two-commit fix-naming branch at lines 147-156 never runs against a real repo. test36 only exercises the pure guard() with booleans. It is not a deviation under §B11.2's one-reading rule, though. The binding guard text (§B8) is "unless the freeze-audit record (§B11.2) is committed", and the code meets that literally. The protocol reads two ways on this point: §B11.2 item 3 says "Freeze audit: once, after the freeze record is committed", while the summary table (line 39) says "one pinned audit per freeze record". §B11.2 item 1 covers this case: "Where the text admits more than one reading, the reading of the code that passed the pre-launch code-review checkpoint stands ... only a later protocol can resolve it", and "Code may change only to match the text." So the proposed check() change is not a permitted §B11.2 fix while the result stands. The gap is reachable only if a fix reverses the committed STOP (5a733be), and the author is told before the next step in that case (§B11.2 item 4).
findings.fix: No code change now. Have the freeze-audit record itself (data, not code) name the freeze-record commit (5a733be) and the blob it audited. Log the once vs per-record ambiguity as §B11.2 requires. If a §B11.2 fix reverses the stop, the author decides whether a second freeze audit of the new record runs before any gate stage. Optionally add a test-only real-repo case for check()'s two-commit branch; tests/ is outside V5.CODE_PATHS, so code identity does not change.

findings.issue: When a stochastic row fails, verdict() returns only 'FAIL (stochastic rows; route stop → E)'. It does not record the v3 label 'PASS, deterministic-only', which §B11.1 requires next to the v5 FAIL.
findings.skeptic_reason: Reproduced (scratchpad v5codereview/verdict_check.py, re-run): with deterministic PASS and stochastic FAIL, verdict() returns {'outcome': 'FAIL (stochastic rows; route stop → E)', 'failed': ['P10a-2']} with no v3 label (metanet_v5_gate.py:302-303). §B11.1: "v3's 'PASS, deterministic-only' is recorded under its v3 label but counts as a v5 FAIL for the route". v3 §0.3 (lines 54-58) lists "a stochastic row fails under F̂" and "... under F̂_T" among the deterministic-only cases. The route decision is correct. The omission is a missing label in the output, and the gate cannot run under the committed STOP, so this is a note. Side issue seen in the same reproduction: verdict() requires the gate_sto provenance stamp (line 295) before it reads the deterministic result. A deterministic FAIL therefore raises SystemExit unless the stochastic stage was also run. That is a crash path only.
findings.fix: Add a 'v3_label' to the stochastic-FAIL branch: 'PASS, deterministic-only (stochastic row failed under F-hat)', or 'F-hat_T' when spread_used == 'Tobit'. This matches the text, so it is a permitted change. Alternatively, write the label into the committed gate-outcome record. Extend test_v5_gate_bindings_and_verdict to check it.

findings.issue: Capacity-grid slices carry no provenance. grid_rows() and spread_v5() read any grid_{seed}_c2_XX.json present, with no check of code identity or plant parameters. Stops, ensemble checks and the CMA summary are all identity-checked at finalize; grids are not.
findings.skeptic_reason: grid_job (metanet_postcal.py:325-326) writes only the rows. grid_rows (metanet_v5_freeze.py:277-284) checks only that the files exist. finalize checks code identity for stops and the CMA summary (424-425) and for ensemble_checks (457), but not for the grids. The scenario needs an operator to skip grid-run in a re-run. grid_run deletes old slices first (598-599), and §B11.2 lists "the grids" in the mandatory full re-run. The v5 raw directory holds 0 grid files today. Under §B11.2, "Code may change only to match the text", and a provenance manifest is defensive, not a text match.
findings.fix: Operational: in any §B11.2 re-run, always run grid-run before ensemble/finalize, and check that the slice mtimes postdate freeze_stops.json. Add the manifest only if it is part of an approved fix.

findings.issue: _clean() converts numpy scalars with .item() before its non-finite check, so a numpy NaN or inf passes through. The json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) calls at lines 393 (freeze_stops) and 661 (finalize) then raise. This is a crash path only; it never writes a wrong value.
findings.skeptic_reason: Reproduced: _clean({'a': np.float64('nan'), 'b': [np.float64('inf')], 'c': float('nan')}) gives {'a': nan, 'b': [inf], 'c': None}, and json.dumps(..., allow_nan=False) then raises ValueError. That is because line 577-578 returns x.item() before the non-finite check at 581. The failure is a crash only (lines 393, 661) and never writes a wrong value. The committed STOP record was written without hitting it.
findings.fix: If it ever triggers: v = float(x); return v if math.isfinite(v) else None, for np.floating and float alike. A crash that blocks the required record commit (§B8 step 6) would then be a text-match fix.

findings.issue: The grid batch, and the gate draws batch (metanet_v5_gate.py:334), use max_workers=32. §B12 caps grid and member jobs at 16 processes.
findings.skeptic_reason: Confirmed for the grid: metanet_v5_freeze.py:602 uses max_workers=32, against §B12 "Grid and member jobs may use up to 16 processes". This is inherited from v4 (metanet_postcal.py:564). For the gate draws (metanet_v5_gate.py:334) the claim is weaker: §B12 states no process count for the gate row, and "member jobs" more naturally means the ensemble checks and grids, not the nominal's gate draws. Each slice and each day is deterministic and independent, so results cannot change. Under the STOP, grid-run never ran.
findings.fix: Set max_workers=16 in grid_run (this matches the text), or record the deviation. Leave the gate draws as they are unless the author reads 'member jobs' as covering them.

findings.issue: The §B5 head-cell report counts an episode with no congested run through cell 26 (head_cell returns None, i.e. 'none') as a day whose P_1 head lies 'outside cells 28-31'. This inflates days_P1_head_outside_28_31 with days that have no head at all. The report is report-only, so the verdict is unaffected.
findings.skeptic_reason: The behaviour is reproduced. In my own synthetic run, with one P_1 episode and no congested cell, head_report gives per_day {'B1': [None]} and days_P1_head_outside_28_31 == ['SYN'], from the condition at metanet_v5_freeze.py:269. Whether this is a deviation is debatable. §B5 says '"none" if no run; and the count of days whose P_1 head lies outside cells 28–31'. A missing head can be read as 'not inside 28-31', so the text arguably has two readings, and under §B11.2 the code's reading stands. The per-day list keeps the None, so no information is lost. The section is report-only, and in the committed freeze record (stop_detail/P11-k/head_cells) there are 0 None heads and 0 outside days, so the actual report is unaffected.
findings.fix: Optional, for clarity in later protocols: report the None days separately (days_P1_head_none) and count only existing heads outside 28-31. Disclose the convention; do not change it post-result.

findings.issue: The pure members() rule is dead code in production. The real rule is inlined in ensemble_checks (metanet_v5_freeze.py:490-500) and finalize (:459-468), so test_members_rule tests a function the pipeline never calls. members() also looks up checks by int seed, while the production checks dict (ensemble_checks.json) is keyed by str(seed). If it were ever wired to the stored checks, it would silently return no gridded candidates and no members.
findings.skeptic_reason: Confirmed. members() (metanet_v5_gate.py:40-50) is called only from tests/test_metanet_v5.py:205. Production inlines the rule: ensemble_checks (freeze.py:476-504) builds 'gridded' with the short-circuit checks 1-3, and finalize (freeze.py:459-468) takes as members the gridded seeds with a usable spread. That inlined rule matches §B6 ('only the first 2 candidates that pass checks 1–3 get a capacity grid'; members pass 1–4). Reproduced: members(cands, {7192012: all True}) gives gridded [7192012], while the same dict after a JSON round-trip gives {'gridded': [], 'members': []}. The key mismatch is latent because the function is not wired in, but test_members_rule gives no coverage of the production rule. Moot for this run: the route stopped, so the ensemble step never ran.
findings.fix: Either have ensemble_checks/finalize call members() with checks keyed by str(seed) (normalise inside members() via checks.get(str(c['seed']), checks.get(c['seed'], {}))), or delete members() and test the inlined rule in ensemble_checks/finalize with stubbed stephalving/p11/screen/spread_v5.

findings.issue: stephalving_pass divides by J5(T) without a guard, so a frozen point with J5(T) == 0.0 raises ZeroDivisionError and crashes the freeze 'stops' stage instead of returning a verdict. In practice this is unreachable: J5 = 0 needs a perfect fit on every row.
findings.skeptic_reason: Reproduced: stephalving_pass((0.0, 0.0), (0.2, 0.2), sets, sets) raises ZeroDivisionError from line 31 (`abs(j5[1]-j5[0])/j5[0]`). J_v4 = 0 at line 32 would do the same. It is unreachable in practice: J5 = 0 needs every row's items to be 0, including the realism NRMSE rows on real data. In this run step-halving passed with J5 = 0.2913, so it has no effect on the result.
findings.fix: Use a guarded relative change: r = 0 if both values are 0, inf if only the T value is 0 (which gives FAIL), and disclose the convention. This is low priority.

findings.issue: Test 25 implements only the per-item upper bounds, which hold by construction because every item is capped at its reference value. Three protocol-required parts are missing: the J5(out) − J5(ref) bound over the listed rows, the comparison with the same day without its P_k episodes at a drawn s_0, and the report of the violation share and the largest P7b + P7c increase. The stub also makes most of the B_k rows trivially safe. B2 'matched' is always None (line 91), so P5a-2 and P7a-2 are always 1. The model C4 equals the real C4 (line 88), so P5a-1 is only ever 0 or 1. 'matched' is the first model episode rather than the one-to-one onset match (line 87). The pure variant (tests/test_metanet_v5.py:96-106) draws t_c (line 104) but never uses it.
findings.skeptic_reason: The gaps are real. test25_e2e (tests/test_metanet_j5_eval.py:298-321) asserts only -1e-12 <= x <= cap per item. It has no J5(out) − J5(ref) bound, no comparison with the same day at a drawn s_0, and no report of the violation share or the largest P7b + P7c increase, all of which §B10 test 25 requires. The _install stub hard-codes B2 'matched': None and 'c4': None (line 91), so P5a-2 and P7a-2 are always 1. It also takes 'matched' as model_b1[0] rather than the one-to-one onset match (line 87). The pure variant draws t_c and never uses it. Two qualifications. (1) One factual slip: P5a-1 is not 'only ever 0 or 1'. With model C4 = real C4, dq = 0, but taper(0, don) = t, which lies strictly between 0 and 1 for 45 < |don| < 90 min, so intermediate values occur. (2) The missing assertions cannot expose a code defect. Every target item is bounded by construction: capped() lies in [0, 1], taper keeps [0, 1], and p3_item is at most 1 + ε because shaping() is at most 1. The (k, d) and day references are exactly those maxima, so claims 1-2 and the J5-difference bound follow algebraically. The no-P_k comparison at s_0 also only adds increases on rows §B1.6 lists (P3-k through s, P7b, P7c, P8g, X-k). The real loss is the protocol-required report, a missing disclosure rather than a correctness risk. Downgraded to note.
findings.fix: Either implement the remaining test 25 parts or record the departure. Implementing them means: build the (k, d)- and day-reference outcomes through day_items, assert the J5-difference bound and the s_0 comparison, and print the violation share and the max P7b + P7c increase. Derive B2 'matched' and c4 from match_episodes on the real longest episode, using a model C4 that differs from the real one. Drop the unused t_c. Otherwise, record in the freeze-audit record that test 25 is item-level only, with the by-construction argument.

findings.issue: Test 24's end-to-end case does not pass through the observation operator, which the protocol requires. test24_e2e stubs Q.model_day and Q.model_speeds (lines 92-93), so the zero-cost property is never checked through model_speeds → model_pairs → model_day (c4, merge, matching). The pure item variant (tests/test_metanet_v5.py:307-317) also stops at the item level, and its docstring says 'pending'.
findings.skeptic_reason: test24_e2e_zero_cost_and_unbacked monkeypatches Q.model_day and Q.model_speeds (tests/test_metanet_j5_eval.py:92-93). The zero-cost property is therefore never exercised 'through the inverse observation operator', as §B10 test 24 requires. The pure variant (test_metanet_v5.py test24_zero_cost_items) stops at item level. I re-ran scratchpad/v5codereview/j5_zero.py, which uses unstubbed model_day, model_speeds and model_pairs, synthetic real series, model = real × MPH, and cells 26-28 and 33 at 1.1·ρ_cr on the real episodes. Result: 200 trials with 0 nonzero target/P8g items. The code is correct and only the test is missing, so note.
findings.fix: Add the unstubbed variant to the suite: stub only I.event_station and I.element_flow, build the real side with F.day_events and F.merge_section plus a JSON round-trip, and assert that every target and P8g item is 0. Add the no-backing companion through the same path.

findings.issue: Unscored items (None, from NRMSE rows with < 100 pairs, P1c_h, P7c) are silently dropped from the row means (metanet_j5.py:180). They are never counted in the J5 parts or the restart reports. The protocol requires them to be counted.
findings.skeptic_reason: Protocol §B1.3 (realism bullet list): 'v3's ≥ 100-pair rule applies to every NRMSE. An unscored item is left out of its row mean and counted.' V.nrmse returns None below 100 pairs (metanet_events.py:24-29). J.j5 drops None (metanet_j5.py:180), and parts (metanet_j5_eval.py:162-164) holds only row means, J_d, any_creditable_B1 and model_active_days. A grep for 'unscored' or 'scored' in the v5 job modules finds no count, and best_rows in metanet_v5_calibrate.py:248 is parts as-is. The leave-out half is implemented; the 'counted' half is a missing report. It cannot change J5 or the route, so note.
findings.fix: Add per-row None counts to parts[pidx] (e.g. 'unscored': {r: sum(x is None for x in v)}). Carry them into best_rows and the restart JSON, and report them for the nominal in the freeze record. Restricting the counts to the NRMSE rows (P1a_h, P1b_h, P1a_ff, P1b_ff, P1c_h) satisfies the protocol sentence.

findings.issue: The §B1.7 'caps ×2/3 and ×4/3' sensitivity also scales CAP_ONSET. The onset cap is not one of the caps the protocol lists for this sensitivity; it is fixed to the match window. At ×4/3 the variant breaks the identity 'onset cap = unmatched score = match window': a creditable match at |Δonset| = 90 min scores 90/120 = 0.75 on P4, while a slightly later, unmatched onset scores 1. The reported caps sensitivity therefore differs from the pre-registered one. It is report-only and cannot select a plant or change the route.
findings.skeptic_reason: I reproduced the mechanism. _variant.CAPS includes CAP_ONSET (metanet_v5_freeze.py:514), and under {'caps': 4/3}, CAP_ONSET = 120. Real (100,120): a creditable match at Δonset = 90 min scores 0.75 on P4, while a model onset 95 min away, unmatched, scores 1.0, a 0.25 jump at the match window. Under 2/3, matches between 60 and 90 min score 1, the same as unmatched. §B1.7's 'Caps' bullet lists six caps (duration, Q_dis, P5c, extent, P1a, P1b) as '3 × the row's gate tolerance'. The onset cap gets its own bullet, defined by an identity: 'Onset cap 90 min = P4's score for an unmatched episode = the match window'. It is also not 3 × P4's 15-min tolerance. So the natural reading of 'the caps at ×2/3 and ×4/3' excludes it, but the protocol does not say so explicitly, hence 'partly'. It is report-only and never selects a plant. sensitivities.json does not exist yet in the v5 raw dir, so it can be corrected before the sensitivities are first run.
findings.fix: Remove CAP_ONSET from _variant.CAPS, so that the onset cap stays tied to the 18-bin match window, before sensitivities() is first run. If it is kept, disclose in sensitivities.json that the onset cap was scaled and that ×4/3 makes P4 non-monotone at the match window.

findings.issue: loo_nulls (the P1c^h leave-one-day-out nulls) and f_mask (F_d for the realism rows) have no unit test, although protocol test 31 requires checking that the P1c nulls leave out day d. test31_hinges (tests/test_metanet_v5.py:23-31) tests only the hinge and floor formulas, and grep finds no test that references loo_nulls or f_mask.
findings.skeptic_reason: A grep of tests/ for loo_nulls and f_mask finds nothing. test31_hinges (tests/test_metanet_v5.py:23-31) covers only the hinge, floor and realism formulas, while §B10 test 31 requires 'the P1c nulls leave out day d'. test29 snapshots only the stored facts constants. I re-ran scratchpad/v5codereview/j5_loo.py (6 days × 17 stations, random speeds and masks): loo_nulls(v, mv, d) equals metanet_gate.nulls() on the other days with NaN equality for every d. f_mask gave 145 bins, starting at EV0 = 12, with the ±6-bin (±30 min) exclusion around the episode. The code is correct and the protocol-required test is missing, so note.
findings.fix: Add the j5_loo.py comparison as a unit test (stub C.load_data with the other days and compare with G.nulls()). Add an f_mask test that checks W_d removal, the ±6-bin exclusion at any pair, and no bins before EV0.

findings.issue: Test 40 lacks several protocol clauses. Missing: the disclosed residuals (head at 26 with a zone over 27-28 → creditable; head at 27 with a one-cell zone over 28 → creditable; P_2 head at 32 with a one-cell zone over 33 → creditable); 'a backed extra does not make an unbacked overlapping episode creditable, and P3-k stays 1 + ε' through day_items; 'an unbacked extra does not strip a backed P3-k hit (it can take a P4/P5a/P7a match by nearer onset, and that item then scores 1)'; the H1 spill-back case.
findings.skeptic_reason: test40_creditability_head_rule (tests/test_metanet_v5.py:40-51) does omit the listed §B10 test 40 clauses. Several omissions are immaterial, though. creditable() reads only the congested-cell matrix in the episode's own qualifying bins. Each residual (head at 26 with a zone over 27-28; head at 27 with a one-cell zone over 28), and the H1 spill-back to cell 25, all reduce to 'cells 26, 27, 28 congested', which the first assert already covers. The P_2 head at 32 with a zone over 33 reduces to 'cell 33 congested', also asserted. The clauses that are genuinely missing are the day-level ones. (a) A backed extra does not make an unbacked overlapping episode creditable, and P3-k stays 1 + ε. This is only covered piecewise, by s_override in test28 and test_p3_items. (b) An unbacked extra does not strip a backed hit and takes the nearer-onset P4/P5a/P7a match, scoring 1. No test covers this. Behaviour is correct: j5_indep.py exercises random backing modes and multiple episodes per day, with 0 mismatches on 300 new-seed days.
findings.fix: Add (a) and (b) as day_items-level asserts on the e2e fixture. For (b), assert the P3-k value, the P4 item = 1 for the match taken by the nearer non-creditable episode, and the pooled P11-k share < 50 % via Q.p11_day on the same day. Optionally list the residual and H1 cases as explicitly named asserts for traceability.

findings.issue: The test 33 audit covers the J5 evaluator, the CMA-ES driver and the screen. It does not cover the §4.7 grid with its J_d selector (postcal.grid_job with jd=V5.evaluator()), ensemble selection or the premise check, which the protocol lists. Its forbidden-path filter also checks only 'val_data' and 'gate_*' strings; the raw validation-date files are not checked.
findings.skeptic_reason: test33 (tests/test_metanet_j5_eval.py:202-253) exercises only J5Eval.__call__, V5.restart and FZ.screen. §B10 test 33 also names 'the §4.7 grid and its selector J_d, ensemble selection, ... and the premise check'. The forbidden-path filter (line 252) matches only 'val_data' and 'gate_det', 'gate_draw' and 'gate_sto', not 'the raw validation-date files', which the protocol explicitly lists. A grep of metanet_v5_freeze, metanet_v5_calibrate, metanet_j5_eval, metanet_v5_facts and metanet_postcal finds no load_val, val_data or F11 access, apart from the F8-only read at metanet_v5_freeze.py:165. grid_job (metanet_postcal.py:266-325) reads only C.load_data and the calibration days' event_pairs and day_events. No leak is known, so this is a coverage gap only: note.
findings.fix: Extend the open/key-access audit to cover grid_job(jd=<stub J5Eval>) with a stubbed simf, the ensemble step and the premise check. Make the filter also flag any Mayfly cache path whose date is not among the facts' 22 calibration days.

findings.issue:
Two parts of test 35 are missing:
- J_d equals the per-day form;
- the §4.7 selector uses J_d with the old tie rule.
The v5 grid hook in grid_job (J_d, b1cells_qual, cred_overlap_k; metanet_postcal.py:302-320) is also untested.
findings.skeptic_reason:
A grep of tests/ finds no call of capacity_factors(..., selector='J_d') or grid_job(jd=...). The only J_d assert is J5Eval's batch list (test_metanet_j5_eval.py:372), and test35_facts_hash (test_metanet_v5.py:114) covers only the hash part of §B10 35.

By reading, the selector key (metanet_freeze.py:182) keeps the old tie rule (hypot to (1,1), then c1), and j_day == j5 on day rows (metanet_j5.py:187-189). The route stopped before §4.7, so nothing recorded depends on this. It becomes required if any audit fix reverses the stop.

test31_hinges (test_metanet_v5.py:23) never calls loo_nulls. test40 (line 40) covers cell patterns only. test41 (test_metanet_j5_eval.py:140) uses a B2 real-inactive evaluator.

No defect:
- I re-ran j5_loo.py: loo_nulls(v, mv, d) equals metanet_gate.nulls() on the other days, for every d of 6 synthetic days.
- By reading, the test-40 interplay clauses hold by construction: p3_item hits only on a creditable overlap (metanet_j5.py:70), and s_override sets s=1 on any overlap (line 142).

Two of the three gaps are not real gaps.

(1) The 'both-None extents' P7b branch is unreachable. extent() always returns a station string: it starts at `start` and returns ext (metanet_gate.py:139-152, identical at the tag). So the 'escaped' mutant (requiring m_ext is not None) is an equivalent mutant, not a test weakness.

(2) The ensemble-candidate step-halving line is textually unchanged from the tag; it only moved under `if ctx is None` (git diff metanet-v4-stop..HEAD). A bit-for-bit risk there is negligible.

(3) The tag running against the current helper modules is true, but test 30(a) is defined as a gate refactor test.

A real but small weakness the finding missed: test30a catches any ValueError from the tag as 'the latent crash' (test_metanet_gate_refactor.py:184-185) without checking its cause, so a different tag-only ValueError would be skipped silently. Only 1 of 30 worlds crashes.
findings.fix: Drop the both-None clause. Narrow the except in test30a to the empty-S1-window crash: assert np.convolve's 'v cannot be empty' message, or check that the world has an empty P9 window. Optionally add one world whose plant seed is an ensemble candidate.

findings.issue: The extended test 22 (no v5 job writes to a v3 or v4 path) has no unit or static counterpart for the v5 modules, the way v4 test22 has for the v4 modules. Enforcement is at runtime only: exact v3/v4 manifest checks after every stage, plus the committed-CODE_PATHS check for repo files.

The gate guard's freeze-audit condition is not tied to any freeze record. check() sets audit=True whenever docs/lab/day_pattern/metanet_v5_freeze_audit.json is tracked and clean. It does not check which freeze record (commit or blob) the audit covered, or that the audit was committed after that record. After a §B11.2 fix re-run that reverses the stop (the case this audit can trigger), a second freeze record, once named by a fix record, would pass the guard on the first record's audit, which reviewed the old code. An audit file committed before the freeze record would also pass. verdict() (line 292) also reads FREEZE5 without the tracked/unchanged check, and takes the PASS vs 'PASS, substitute spread' label from it.
findings.skeptic_reason: The guard does what §B8's text says: 'unless the freeze-audit record (§B11.2) is committed'. With the route at 'STOP (in-sample screen)', guard() refuses at line 59 before the audit check, so this code is reachable only if a §B11.2 fix reverses the stop. In that case the question is whether a second freeze record needs its own audit. The protocol has two readings: §B11.2 item 3 says 'Freeze audit: once, after the freeze record is committed', while the header table says 'one pinned audit per freeze record'. Under §B11.2 item 1, the checkpointed code's reading stands (any committed audit), so this is not a deviation. The case 'audit committed before the freeze record' cannot happen now: the record was committed at 5a733be and no audit file exists yet. It is true that verdict() (line 292) reads FREEZE5 without the tracked and unchanged check, but exploiting that needs a hand edit of the committed record, and it would only change the PASS label.
findings.fix: No code change is needed now. When writing the freeze-audit record, put freeze_record_commit = 5a733be and the git blob hash of metanet_v5_calibration.json in it, and log the 'once' vs 'per freeze record' ambiguity as disclosed. If a fix reverses the stop, the audit record then names which record it covered. Binding the guard to it, and the tracked check in verdict(), belong to a later protocol or a disclosed hardening.

findings.issue: Worker processes never check the code identity; only the drivers do, at launch. The CMA-ES restart worker (metanet_v5_calibrate.restart) and the grid worker import whatever is on disk when the scheduler starts them. evaluator() runs pre_batch_checks, which checks only the manifests, not code_commit(). Jobs launched late import that disk state, including uncommitted edits by a sibling session to CODE_PATHS modules: the grid has 41 jobs on 32 workers, and the CPU guard can hold any job back. The draws workers do check. Grid outputs carry no identity stamp. grid_rows(), which feeds spread_v5 in finalize and ensemble_checks, reads them without the provenance check that stops, the summary and ensemble_checks.json all get. So a stale or mixed grid could decide stop 5 under a record that names the current code.
findings.skeptic_reason: The code reading is accurate. restart() and the grid worker (metanet_v5_freeze.py:635-638) never call code_commit(), and grid_rows() only checks that the files exist. No committed text requires per-worker identity checks on calibration-side jobs, though. v4 §A6 (6), 'only committed gate code reads validation-day real data', applies to gate code, and the gate draws workers do check (metanet_v5_gate.py:268-271). In this run: thermal.csv shows launch events at 0.0 s and 0.5 s, with running=8 by 0.5 s, so all 8 restarts imported the code right after the driver's code_commit(). That identity, 3d4402f, equals today's code_commit() (reproduced). finalize compared cma_summary's code_commit and freeze_stops' code with the current identity. The grid never ran, because the route stopped at stop 4. So the outcome is unaffected. The remaining risk is a sibling session's uncommitted edit during a future re-run grid (41 jobs on 32 workers). §B11.2 says 'Code may change only to match the text', so this is not a deviation to fix now.
findings.fix: Disclose it in the audit record. In a later protocol, or as a disclosed hardening before any re-run: pass the driver's identity to every job, have restart(), the grid worker and timing refuse a mismatch, stamp the identity into cma_restart_*.json and grid_*.json, and have grid_rows, _batch and finalize refuse stamps that differ from the current identity.

findings.issue: code_commit() fails open. Any git error leaves stdout empty, which is read as 'clean', and the identity becomes the empty string ''. Every launch path also calls committed(), which raises on a git error, so the risk today is low. But freeze_stops() (code stamp), stops_passed() and finalize() all compare identities that could both be '' if git fails while committed() is skipped or succeeds transiently.
findings.skeptic_reason: Reproduced. With C.REPO pointed at a non-git scratch directory, V5.code_commit() returns '' and raises nothing, because lines 167-170 read .stdout and never check returncode. On the same directory, committed() raises SystemExit. Every J5 path goes through evaluator(), which calls committed(), and every stage's __exit__ calls post_batch_checks(), which also calls committed(). The identities stored by this run are real SHAs (3d4402f), so a transient '' would mismatch and refuse rather than pass. There is no effect on the current outcome.
findings.fix: In code_commit(), raise SystemExit when git status or git log returns non-zero, or when the identity is not a 40-hex SHA. Apply it with any re-run, or adopt it as a disclosed hardening.

findings.issue: The capacity-grid batch, and the gate's draws batch, run with max_workers=32. Protocol v5 §B12 caps grid and member jobs at 16 processes. Results are unaffected (the jobs are independent and deterministic). It is still a code-vs-text deviation, and §B11.2 lets code change only to match the text.
findings.skeptic_reason: For the grid there is a literal mismatch: metanet_v5_freeze.py:602 sets max_workers=32, and §B12 Layout says 'Grid and member jobs may use up to 16 processes.' The grid never ran in this run (route STOP at stop 4), and its jobs are independent and deterministic, so no output changes. The sentence also sits in the compute-projection paragraph. For gate draws (metanet_v5_gate.py:334) it is ambiguous whether 'member jobs' covers them: they are gate jobs, the nominal's included. So the checkpointed reading stands.
findings.fix: Disclose it in the audit record. Set the grid to max_workers=16 before any re-run reaches the grid. Log the gate-draws reading as a disclosed ambiguity.

findings.issue: The v5 facts record the git blob hashes of the reused v3 and v4 facts files, but no v5 job checks them at use. The screen reads F8 floors from C.FACTS (metanet_v5_freeze.py:165), and other paths read the v4 facts and record. A committed change to either file would only change the code identity; nothing compares it with the recorded blobs. Both files match today.
findings.skeptic_reason: Not a deviation. §B8 step 4 only requires 'Both git blob hashes are recorded in the v5 facts', and that is done: reused_facts_blobs = {v3: c3ed7041..., v4: 8b8dc558...}, which equal `git hash-object` of both files today. Their last commits (91603bf and 549ab7b) predate v5. Both files are in CODE_PATHS, so an uncommitted edit blocks code_commit() at every driver and stage, and a committed edit changes the identity that freeze_stops, finalize and the gate start records compare. Checking at the point of use would only be a hardening.
findings.fix: Optional hardening for a later protocol: in evaluator() and screen(), compare the git hash-object of C.FACTS and C.FACTS_V4 with facts['reused_facts_blobs'] and refuse on a mismatch. State in the audit record that the blobs matched at audit time.

critic_gaps.area: Freeze-audit scope (§B11.2 item 3, §B8 step 6): the outputs under audit were reviewed by no lens
critic_gaps.why: Each §B11.2 audit runs once and cannot be repeated. Its record will be read as having audited the freeze outcome, but by construction it did not reproduce or review that outcome or the unchanged imported modules. The audit record should say so, and include the consistency checks above, before E is recorded.

critic_gaps.area: §B11.2 item 4 (W13 strict) and item 2: outcome labels after a fix are not implemented
critic_gaps.why: The freeze audit can open exactly this path: a fix plus a full re-run that reverses the stop. A post-fix record or gate verdict without these labels would present a KILL-only or post-fix result as an ordinary GO-capable PASS, which is the integrity failure W13 strict exists to prevent.

critic_gaps.area: §B11.2 item 1 re-run path on the calibration side (no archive, no fix-record precondition)
critic_gaps.why: This is the next path if the audit finds a deviation. 'Both outcomes are logged' and the audit trail of the original STOP (the 7 non-nominal restarts, their histories and states) would be lost on the first re-run, and an unrecorded re-run is not blocked on the calibration side.

critic_gaps.area: Freeze record contents and provenance (v3 §8.3, §4.5, §4.8; v4 §A13; §B8 Paths; §B13 item 1; checkpoint promise)
critic_gaps.why: 'Every v3/v4 text not amended here applies word for word.' These items are report-only and cannot change the route, but the audit and any later result (including a post-fix one) depend on them. The identity of the producing code can now be recovered only from ledger rows.

critic_gaps.area: §B1.7 and §B1.4 sensitivities: implemented but never scheduled or run
critic_gaps.what: metanet_v5_freeze.sensitivities() exists (lines 545-557, CLI 'sensitivities'), but no step in the launch order in metanet_v5_impl_checkpoint.md runs it. The ledger has no sensitivities row, and the raw dir /home/catalin/work/phd/vsl_lab_runs/day_pattern/metanet_v5/ has no sensitivities.json. §B1.4 says 'The sensitivities ε = 0 and ε = 1 are reported (§B1.7)', and §B1.7 re-scores 'the 8 restarts' best points'. Neither is conditioned on a PASS; §B8 step 8 restricts only the profiles to 'only after a PASS'. The function also re-scores only the admissible restarts, and its caps variant has the j5-05 defect.
critic_gaps.why: After the STOP, nothing will produce these pre-registered report-only numbers unless the author decides how §B8 step 8 reads after a pre-look stop. That is a §B11.2 ambiguity to log, not to fix silently.

critic_gaps.area: §B8 step 7 and v3 §8.3: committing the gate outcome conflicts with the first-record guard
critic_gaps.what: No v5 code commits the gate outcome. verdict() only returns a dict, and the outputs stay in the raw dir. v3 §8.3, however, has the calibration record 'committed in two stages: the freeze ... then the gate results', and §B8 step 7 says 'Commit the outcome, then run the gate audit'. If the outcome goes into metanet_v5_calibration.json, check() sets first = len(git log -- record) == 1 (metanet_v5_gate.py:147-148), and guard() requires stage == 'freeze' (line 57). Every later gate stage would then be refused: member runs, stochastic rows, or a §B11.2 post-look re-run. The exception is a fix record whose freeze_record_commit names that non-freeze commit.
critic_gaps.why: This is reachable only if a fix reverses the stop and the route reaches the gate. Without a defined place for the gate outcome, a session could commit it so that the guard locks the remaining pre-registered gate stages, or misuse a fix record to get past the guard.
